newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Berisha seeks support, Vefa to repay investors.
newsitem.headline: Berisha seeks support, Vefa to repay investors.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha, under attack by thousands of investors who lost money in fraudulent pyramid investment schemes, stepped up a campaign to win back popular support on Wednesday.
Amid heavy security, he travelled to this central town to explain his government's handling of the scandal which has engulfed Europe's poorest nation.
Albania has been swept by a month of riots and protests by thousands of investors who lost large sums when the fraudulent pyramid schemes collapsed in January.
Berisha, on his third whistle-stop visit since Saturday, addressed 1,500 hand-picked supporters in a sports hall. They applauded and chanted his name as he strode in.

"I came to thank them for the way they've dealt with their losses. We cannot pay their debts but we can intervene to speed up growth and ensure economic recovery of the people," he said before entering.

Asked about persistent anti-government protests in the southern port of Vlore, he said: "They are very brave. They have had huge losses. I am very sad but I am sure I will find a common language with them."
Berisha has vowed to go to Vlore, where three people died during unrest last week, but he has not set a date.
Residents in the region around Vlore invested heavily in the Gjallica fund, which collapsed with no assets. Thousands of people lost money.

Five high-risk schemes, in which an estimated $1 to $2 billion had been invested, collapsed in January. Investors have blamed Berisha and his government for failing to regulate the schemes and have demanded compensation.
Berisha congratulated the people of Elbasan for not joining the violence which rocked many towns and cities.

"You did not allow your despair and loss to be manipulated, giving proof to the great value of your citizen tradition," he said. Berisha has accused the opposition Socialist Party, the former communists, of stirring up trouble.
He said the only common thread among all Albanian political parties over the past four years has been their silence over the dangers of the pyramid investment schemes.
"Because of their responsibility for silence they should have cooperated closely to resolve these problems. That did not happen," he said referring to the opposition Socialists.
The Socialists have refused repeatedly to meet the ruling Democrats to discuss the pyramid scandal.
In Tirana, Vefa Holding, Albania's biggest holding company which froze client accounts last month, said it would pay back all deposits by small investors immediately.
Vefa, which has 240 businesses and 80,000 investors, said that from today it would make full repayment to all investors who had put up to $5,000 in the company.
The decision was taken by company President Vehbi Alimucaj, and it would take two to three weeks to pay back all small investors, representing about 60 percent of Vefa's clients.
The Vefa move was intended to calm investors' nerves and disperse hundreds of people who have waited outside its offices for the past month hoping to get their money back.
Investors will get only their capital investment and none of the interest due, company representative Arben Iliazi told Reuters.
The collapse of the fraudulent schemes left many Albanians penniless and triggered a popular outcry against the government.

Vefa is a household word in Albania. Its name is on foods, supermarkets and a television station. After pyramid companies collapsed, Vefa and three other investment firms froze client accounts, fearing a run of withdrawals.
After small investors who wish to withdraw funds have done so, investors who put in $5,000 to $10,000 will be able to withdraw money, and then those who invested $10,000 to $20,000, Vefa said.
